title: Values, Names and Variables
learningObjectives: Define a value as data a program can use, including numbers, text strings, and true/false Boolean values.
Explain how values represent information used in calculations, decisions, messages, comparisons, and other program operations.
Distinguish a value from the name used to refer to it, using examples such as 25 and studentAge.
Define a name as a label that identifies a program element and explain why descriptive names improve readability.
Explain a variable as a named binding through which code refers to a value, rather than treating it only as a physical box.
Identify the declaration keyword, identifier, assignment operator, and value in a JavaScript variable declaration.
Explain that a variable name is an identifier and recognize identifiers in short code examples.
Apply JavaScript naming rules: identifiers cannot begin with a digit, contain spaces, or use reserved keywords.
Explain case sensitivity and distinguish identifiers such as score and Score.
Choose meaningful names such as studentName, totalPrice, and itemCount instead of unclear names.
Use const for a binding that should not be reassigned and explain the restriction it creates.
Use let for a binding that may need a new value and demonstrate reassignment.
Distinguish reassignment of a const binding from changing properties or elements of an object or array it refers to.
Predict the values displayed after a sequence of variable declarations and assignments.
Identify naming mistakes such as leading digits, spaces, reserved words, and inconsistent capitalization.
Correct a simple declaration by choosing a valid identifier and suitable declaration keyword.
Explain how purposeful names make code easier to read, maintain, review, and debug.
Create a JavaScript example that stores related information in separate variables and displays it.
Trace how a value is associated with a variable name and then used in a later expression or statement.
Connect values, names, identifiers, and variables to later topics such as data types, operators, expressions, conditions, loops, and functions.

understand.concept: A value is data such as a number, text or true/false. A variable is a named binding used to refer to a value. Names should describe purpose and follow language-specific rules.
understand.whyItMatters: These ideas form the foundation for learning every programming language.
understand.history: This lesson focuses on transferable programming concepts; detailed language history is taught in the relevant language module.
understand.analogy: It is like writing clear instructions for a task and following them step by step.
understand.analogyLimit: Programming language rules are precise; a computer does not automatically infer ambiguity in casual human instructions.
